messages:
Priya (Support): FYI - AtlasHealth reported a sharp p95 increase on their dedicated pool right after yesterday's rollout, started ~08:10 UTC. p95 jumped from 230ms -> 1.2s.
Jorge (Sales): Oof, they just flagged it to me this morning, asking for ETA on a fix. They're on a committed SLA.
Priya (Support): Logs attached in ticket, summary: increased queuing, a bunch of 429s on model-route A, and slow tail tokens. No errors in model, just latency spikes.
Sara (Product): Can we get an immediate triage: impact (users affected / requests per min), root cause hypothesis, and mitigation options? Sales needs messaging.
Ken (Eng Runtime): Looking at metrics — the spike correlates with a routing change that sent a subset of traffic to v2-quantized. Sequence length distribution for Atlas is higher than expected; v2-quantization increases KV cache pressure. Hypothesis: cache churn causing repeated recompute + small batch sizes.
Mei (Eng Platform): Confirmed: autoscaler didn't spin up extra workers because burst threshold was missed due to smaller sustained QPS.
Alex (SRE): Also saw CPU pin spikes on nodes serving v2-quantized. I scraped recent logs: many small requests arriving concurrently and causing serialization.
Priya (Support): Customer impact: ~6% of requests saw >1s p95; their highest-priority endpoint is affected. They want a rollback if not quick fix.
Jorge (Sales): They asked for a rollback last night, withheld until we confirmed. Need decision point: rollback v2-quantized for Atlas only, or apply platform-side mitigation.
Ken (Eng Runtime): Quick mitigation options: 1) route Atlas back to v1 (safe rollback, immediate) 2) enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for this route (config toggle) 3) temporarily bump reserved workers for Atlas pool.
Sara (Product): What are tradeoffs? Rollback buys time but hides perf improvements. Caching may help quickly if we can toggle per-route. Bumping workers costs $$ but fastest.
Mei (Eng Platform): We can toggle per-route caching via route config now (30s to propagate). Bumping workers requires a commit and might trigger billing alerts. Rollback is a single flag and low-risk.
Ken (Eng Runtime): If we rollback, we should also add a guard to prevent automatic rollout to customers with >avg seq len until we validate quantized path.
Alex (SRE): If we choose route-level caching toggle, we should watch warmup — could spike memory. I'll stand by the patch and monitor.
Sara (Product): OK decision: toggle route-level caching for Atlas as immediate mitigation, open a priority backlog ticket to investigate quantized path edge cases, and schedule a controlled rollback only if mitigation fails within 1 hour. Communicate ETA to customer: 1h for mitigation then next steps.
Jorge (Sales): I'll tell Atlas we're applying a config change now, expect visible improvement in ~5-10m, and we'll update in 30m.
Priya (Support): Implementing caching toggle now -> /config/routes/atlas-health/enabledCaching = true 
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by Mei: route-config-upsert atlas-health caching=true (deploy id dpl-8812).
Mei (Eng Platform): Done, propagated to 3/3 edge clusters.
Ken (Eng Runtime): Observability: p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 360ms within 6 minutes. 429s back to baseline.
Jorge (Sales): Atlas replied: saw improvement, queued follow-up for SLA credit discussion but happy for now. :relieved:
Sara (Product): Next actions (backlog): create ticket PROD-6123 - "Quantized path KV-cache churn with high-seq customers". Must include rollout guard: per-customer sequence length gating + automatic canary. Acceptance criteria: reproduce locally, fix cache eviction policy, add rollout gate + canary, and run perf eval on heavy seq workloads.
Ken (Eng Runtime): I'll own the investigation and draft a spec for rollout gating.
Alex (SRE): I'll add alert refinement to catch this pattern earlier: combine p95 + cache miss rate + node CPU spikes.
Priya (Support): Closing immediate incident. I'll add customer notes and mark ticket high-priority.
Sara (Product): Thanks team. We'll sync in the 11:00 roadmap slot to decide resource priority. Jorge — can you surface SLA pressure if Atlas asks for credits?
Jorge (Sales): Yes, will share details in the sync.
Priya (Support): Thread resolved for now. Keeping PROD-6123 open. :white_check_mark:
